personalityFieldsNote: Every gate references a field that exists today per c1-integration-map.md §1. PlayerPersonality has only archetype and motivation; MentalAttributes has only awareness, decisionMaking, clutch, workEthic, coachability and leadership. There is no `discipline` and no `composure` field — the schema example's PlayerPersonality.discipline and MentalAttributes.composure do not exist and are NOT used anywhere in this file. The nearest real analogues are used instead: discipline-ish -> workEthic / coachability, composure-ish -> clutch, resilience -> Player.competitiveness. Archetype predicates (isEgoArchetype, isFormSensitive, tier, isDramaticInMedia, isMentor, isMoodDependent, isConsistent) are the ready-made hooks already defined on the enum. Motivation rawValues are Money/Winning/Stats/Loyalty/Fame; MotivationState cases are driven/focused/complacent/discouraged — the schema example's "distracted" is not a real case, so `discouraged` is used for every distraction transition.
volumeClassNote: probability.volumeClass is one of: `primary` (a first-order incident that must reconcile against the research base rates), `derived` (a downstream stage of a primary event — league review, exempt-list placement, suspension, appeal, fine, clearing, reinstatement — excluded from the reconciliation so arrests and suspensions are not double-counted), or `preEmployment` (prospect-track events that act on draft position rather than on a roster).

targetLeagueYearVolume.notes: Primary = arrests 38.60 + PED suspensions 16.40 + substances-of-abuse suspensions 1.02 + gambling 1.19. Derived and pre-employment volumes are tracked separately and are NOT part of the base-rate reconciliation.

calibrationSummary:
RECONCILIATION (league = 32 clubs, ~2,240 players under contract in season).
PRIMARY volume = 57.21 events/league-year, split exactly as the research base rates require:
  (a) ARRESTS / CHARGES = 38.60  vs r1-legal.md §0 target 38.6 (league-internal arrest series 2015-2023: mean 38.6, median 38, SD 8.0, range 28-53; recommended generator NegBin(mu=38, var=64)). Category mix follows r1 §1.0b exactly: DUI 10.10 (26%) · domestic violence 5.40 (14%) · non-domestic assault 4.60 (12%) · weapons 4.60 (12%) · drug possession 3.50 (9%) · disorderly/alcohol 3.50 (9%) · theft/fraud 1.50 (4%) · reckless driving 1.50 (4%) · sexual misconduct 0.80 (2%) · homicide 0.40 (1%) · animal 0.30 (0.8%) · misc 2.40 (6.2%). Per-player-season this is 1.72% on a 2,240 denominator and 1.21 incidents per club per year, reproducing r1 §2.6 (30% of clubs clean, 12.2% with three or more).
  (b) PED SUSPENSIONS = 16.40  vs r2 §5.2 target 16.4/yr (82 suspensions in the five years to early 2022). Internal split follows r2 §4.1: 2-game stimulant class 7.00 (43%), 6-game anabolic class 7.05 (43%), 8-game manipulation 0.80 (5%), second violations 1.30 (8%), third-strike banishment 0.25 (1.5%).
  (c) SUBSTANCES-OF-ABUSE SUSPENSIONS = 1.02  vs r2 §5.2 target ~1/yr post-2020 (was 5-10 pre-2020). All of it reaches games through the LAW, never through a positive test, per r2 §2.2-2.3.
  (d) GAMBLING = 1.19, of which suspension-bearing = 0.74 vs r2 §5.3 baseline 0.5-1.0/yr (12-year mean 1.0); the remaining 0.45 is the once-per-decade integrity-sweep trigger (0.10) and the non-disciplinary warning tier (0.35). The sweep sets a wave flag that multiplies the other gambling rates for that league year, reproducing the 0-0-0-0-1-0-0-10-0-0 shape rather than a flat Poisson.
  Primary check: 38.60 + 16.40 + 1.02 + 1.19 = 57.21.
DERIVED volume = 59.10 events/league-year. These are downstream stages of a primary event — league reviews, exempt-list placements, the suspension itself, appeals, fines, programme fines, clearings and reinstatements — and are deliberately EXCLUDED from the reconciliation above so the arrest and suspension counts are not double-counted. Their internal calibration still traces to research: conduct suspensions total 5.30/yr against r2 §5.2's 3-6/yr personal-conduct figure, and the 1-3 game band (2.50) to 6-game band (1.40) ratio reproduces the bimodal histogram in r1 §4.8 (mode 1, median 3, mean 3.39 outside the named categories; mode 6, median 6, mean 5.5 inside them). Fine-track volumes (substances-programme positives at 18.0/yr combined) are flagged userTeamOnly because the source material treats them as confidential to the club and r2 §9.5 records the true rate as unpublished.
PRE-EMPLOYMENT volume = 5.00 events/league-year (pre-draft red flag 3.00, withheld showcase invitation 2.00) vs r1 §5 A10's '2-4 prospects per draft class'. Excluded from the arrest total because the conduct policy reaches these players before they are ever employed and the consequence lands on draft position, not on a roster.
LEGAL DISPOSITIONS are applied as arc forks, not as separate events, using r1 §4.7 verbatim: all arrests 47-50% convicted / 31% dropped / 13-15% diversion, with ~26% of rows never publicly resolved; domestic violence 21-23 / 37 / 36-38 at a 20% unresolved rate; impaired driving 70-71 / 15 / 14 at 15% unresolved. Every arrest event therefore carries a real chance of simply fading out, which r1 §4.7 calls a feature worth shipping deliberately.
POSITIVE EVENTS: 6 of 121 (5%). Below the schema's 15-25% guidance by design — this section covers arrests and league discipline, where the research supports few standalone positives. The positive mass that the research DOES support (31% dropped, 13-15% diversion, the modal zero-game league outcome) is carried inside the resolution arcs of the negative events rather than duplicated as separate catalog entries. K3 carries the positive share for the catalog as a whole.
contentSafetyNote: Per r1-legal.md §6.4: the heavy categories are kept as consequence generators and never render incident detail. Copy names the charge class and the process only — no depiction, no specifics, no victims described. No real people, clubs, outlets, sponsors or league marks appear anywhere; the fictional analogues used are 'the league office', 'the league', 'the conduct policy', 'the substances programme', 'the scouting showcase' and 'the league's annual community award'.
